newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnian leaders sign deal clearing way for aid.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian leaders sign deal clearing way for aid.

text.p: Bosnia's rival presidents on Friday signed a budget agreement demanded by the international community, clearing the way for $100 million in IMF loans and $1 billion or more in international assistance, a senior U.S. official said.

After a meeting in which Secretary of State Madeleine Albright pressured them to act -- and left her pen for them to use -- the Moslem, Serb and Croat presidents "signed it," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burn said of the budget agreement.

Burns said the action cleared the way for the International Monetary Fund to release $100 million in loans and for the international community to schedule a donors conference in Brussels on June 24 that could provide as much as $1.4 billion in assistance for Bosnia's recovery from 44 months of war.

The budget agreement, in which the three presidents settled on macro budget figures for their government, is among a package of economic reform measures the United States and the IMF have demanded Bosnia's leaders sign as evidence that they are integrating their divided country.
"The price of the $100 million is to pass a budget law," Burns told reporters.

Albright, leading a U.S. effort to increase international pressure on key parties to comply with the fraying Bosnia peace agreement, had a 15-minute meeting with the Balkan country's three chiefs -- Moslem Alija Izetbegovic, Croat Kresimir Zubak and Serb Momcilo Krajisnik.
